pr_title: coredump: support forwarding coredumps to containers
pr_body:
Add support for forwarding coredumps to the container in which a process crashed. This will only happen when the container is within a delegated cgroup which also has a new setting, `CoredumpReceive=yes`. This ensures that coredump forwarding is not configured globally,  but that in can be configured per-container or per-container manager.

Fixes: #24426

can you move the two iovw_put_string_field() lines from further up in the function to the end of the function? now that we redirect coredumps like this it's kinda useless doing that work for nothing.
Not 100% sure but I think you can close this one already in the parent process right after calling `send_ucred_and_one_fd()`
i.e. as suggested above, please move the send_ucred_and_one_fd() call after this here
We don't do this anymore now, is that intended?
Yeah, the caller of this function doesn't actually check for specific error codes, so I decided to just leave it out. I think it would be valid for a caller to just check `-EADDRNOTAVAIL` directly.
i think it would be nice to close `pair[0]` here early in the child to communicate to the reader which part of the socket pair is for the parent, and which one for the child
i think we should add some field here btw, that indicates that this has been handed in from the outside. just to make debugging easier. COREDUMP_CONTAINER_HOST=1 or so.

Why is this entering namespaces of `namespace_get_leader` instead of the crashing process?

(The latter seems simpler, so a) I'm wondering, b) it should be noted in the commit message/comment.)

we always want to submit the coredump in the same context as PID 1 inside the container, to make sure the behaviour is as close to the host as possible, where after all the kernel invokes core_pattern also in the same execution context pretty much as PID 1.

Consider he case where systemd runs inside a container, and systemd runs a service with mount namespacing which dies. In that case the coredump should be processed in the environment of PID1 in that container, but certainly not in that possibly super restricted mount namespace of the crashing process.
